# Libadwaita API Reference

> Official GTK 4/libadwaita API documentation, version 1.9.3, including widget classes, interfaces, functions, enums, and developer guides.

Source: https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/
Full documentation: https://github.com/Areo-RGB/transfer/blob/main/libadwaita/llms-full.txt

## Guides and overview

- [Adw – 1](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/): API reference documentation.
- [Adw – 1: Adaptive Layouts](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/adaptive-layouts.html): Libadwaita provides a number of widgets that change their layout based on the available space.
- [Adw – 1: Boxed Lists](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/boxed-lists.html): Libadwaita provides API to implement the boxed lists pattern.
- [Adw – 1: Compiling with Libadwaita](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/build-howto.html): If you need to build Libadwaita, get the source from here and see the README.md file.
- [Adw – 1: Classes Hierarchy](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/classes_hierarchy.html): API reference documentation.
- [Adw – 1: CSS Variables](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/css-variables.html): The Adwaita stylesheet provides a number of predefined CSS variables for colors that can be used from applications.
- [Adw – 1: Initialization](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/initialization.html): Before using Libadwaita, it must be initialized. There are two ways of doing this.
- [Adw – 1: Migrating from Libhandy 1.4 to Libadwaita](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-libhandy-1-4-to-libadwaita.html): Libadwaita is being developed as a successor to Libhandy 1.4. As such, it offers to GTK 4 many features Libhandy was offering to GTK 3.
- [Adw – 1: Migrating to Adaptive Dialogs](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-adaptive-dialogs.html): Libadwaita 1.5 introduces AdwDialog and replacements for AdwMessageDialog, AdwPreferencesWindow and AdwAboutWindow that derive from it.
- [Adw – 1: Migrating to Breakpoints](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/migrating-to-breakpoints.html): Libadwaita 1.4 introduces AdwBreakpoint and new adaptive widgets that can integrate with it, while deprecating the old widgets.
- [Adw – 1: Style Classes](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/style-classes.html): The Adwaita stylesheet provides a number of style classes. They can be applied to widgets to change their appearance.
- [Adw – 1: Styles & Appearance](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/styles-and-appearance.html): Libadwaita applications can use a light or a dark appearance. This can be used to request a darker UI, or to support a system-wide dark style preference if one exists.
- [Adw – 1: Widget Gallery](https://gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org/libadwaita/doc/1-latest/widget-gallery.html): See also: AdwClampLayout, AdwClampScrollable
